chapter: Gene Mayl, Teddy Buckner and the Dixie Flies
title: Yellow Dog Blues as a national hit
summary: The Lark single of Yellow Dog Blues backed with Martinique became a national hit, copied by other bands and Pete Fountain; W.C. Handy wrote Joe to praise it.

bands.name: Joe Darensbourg and His Dixie Flies

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How big a hit was that?

Oh, man, it was a terrific hit. It was sensational. What happened was that the recording company that made it, Lark Records, they sent... It was made as a single, with that tune "Martinique" that the DeParis brothers... They put it on the back of that. Instead of my putting my "Louisiana, Ay-Ai(?)" on the back of that, I made a zillion dollars in royalties on top of "Yellow Dog," you see -- but we put "Martinique" anyway. Both of them was a hit. It started with some... A disk jockey just picked it up, and... He told me afterwards (because I went on tour back there), he says, "I threw that thing in the

wastebasket, then I went back and picked it up because of the title, and started playing it, and I couldn't believe my ears." And he says, "When I put it on the air, inside of two hours, I got more calls and this and that..."
You'll have to forgive me because I'm new in this country. Was it a hit nationally or just...?

Nationally. A lot of the cities was havin' contests. Then... I'm trying to think of... Another...a cover record came out with somebody else's slap-tongue, not as good as me. Even Pete Fountain made a record of it! But he didn't try to slap-tongue because he couldn't, I don't believe. He used a guitar to make that plunking sound. All of these bands and companies was making a cover record of the "Yellow Dog Blues" to sell it. People would come in and ask for "Yellow Dog Blues"...
Was it out of copyright then?
No, no, it was still in copyright. Because I remember, I got a letter from Handy (I don't know what I did with it, it might be home someplace)...
...that was telling me how great it was. He said, "Dear Joe: When I wrote the 'Yellow Dog Blues'... I hear your recording of it, and that's the way I intended this tune to be played when I wrote it."
